name: glitchless
description: Game observability: ranked findings, frame times, errors, where players die, store reviews, revenue and each game's own dashboard, from what real players' sessions measured.

interface.shortDescription: Find what's wrong in your game
interface.longDescription:
Glitchless is observability for games made with Three.js, Phaser, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas, Unity, Godot, Unreal and GameMaker. Connect it and ask about your games in plain words: what's wrong this week, where players die, which error hits the most sessions, whether last night's build fixed the stutter on level 2.

Answers come from what your players' sessions actually measured. Triage ranks findings by how many players they hit, each with its evidence and a suggested fix: frame-time spikes per level and what they correlate with, memory leaks, top errors with their stack and the gameplay right before them, difficulty spikes and rage quits, and version regressions. You can drill into frame times by level, GPU tier and browser, one error, one session's whole timeline, the game's own events and funnels, and bug reports players sent from inside the game, with their screenshots.

For games connected to a store or a payments provider, it reads Steam, Google Play and App Store reviews and vitals next to what Glitchless measured on each build, and RevenueCat or Stripe revenue next to the players who made it.

Each game has its own dashboard in its own terms, and the assistant can read it or design a new one. It can also create a game and make a read-only share link to a board.

You sign in with your Glitchless account and choose the workspace and what the assistant may do. It acts as you, never deletes data and never touches billing or people, and you can disconnect it any time in Settings → Keys & access. You need a Glitchless account (free) with at least one game sending data.

positive.description: Rank what's wrong with a game
positive.prompt: What's wrong with Zoomies this week?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists Zoomies' findings ranked by severity and players affected, each with its evidence: the difficulty spike at the vacuum on level 2 (Dog Park, around x 40, about two thirds of the level's deaths), the TypeError reading 'velocity' that hits about a fifth of sessions, and level 2's stutter from shader compiles in 1.0.0, with 1.1.0 named as the version that removed it.

positive.description: Where players die on a level
positive.prompt: Where do players die most on level 2 of Zoomies, and what kills them?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the spot around x 38 to 43 on level 2 where most deaths happen, its share of the level's deaths (about two thirds), the vacuum as what kills players there, and the level's completion rate.

positive.description: The top error and what came before it
positive.prompt: Which error hits the most Zoomies sessions, and what happened right before it?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the TypeError reading 'velocity' in Player.update, the share of sessions it hits (about a fifth), that it happens on level 2 in both versions, and what came just before it: entering level 2 and, in 1.0.0, the hitches there.

Lists the dashboard's pages (a Zoomies board, then Performance, Errors, Players, Heatmaps, Sessions, Versions and Live Tail) and reads the board's numbers for the window: players, play sessions, frame time, rage quits, findings, levels, where players die in the Dog Park, power-ups and errors.

positive.description: Confirm a fix with real players
positive.prompt: Compare Zoomies 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 over the past week. Did 1.1.0 fix the level 2 stutter?
positive.expected_behavior: Compares 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 side by side and says level 2's hitches went from several a minute in 1.0.0 to none in 1.1.0, while errors and deaths at the vacuum stayed about the same.

negative.prompt: Write a Python function that sorts a list.
What's the weather in Seattle tomorrow?

negative.description: Game recommendation, not the user's own game data
negative.prompt: Recommend a good platformer to play this weekend.

review.commerce_description: Glitchless doesn't sell anything or take payments through ChatGPT. Its tools read and organize the user's own game data.

publication.release_notes: First release: findings, frame times, errors, death hotspots, sessions, events, bug reports, store reviews and vitals, revenue and dashboards for your games, with sign-in to your Glitchless workspace.
